findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:119: align-items() omits -moz-box-align despite display mixins supporting -moz-box, causing fallback browsers to retain stretch alignment instead of vertically centering header and small-action children. Add -moz-box-align: $alignment.

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss:119: align-items() omits -moz-box-align despite display mixins supporting -moz-box, causing fallback browsers to retain stretch alignment instead of vertically centering header and small-action children. Add -moz-box-align: $alignment.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the align-items mixin at line 119 includes -webkit-box-align, -webkit-align-items, -ms-flex-align, -ms-align-items, and align-items, but omits -moz-box-align. Meanwhile, the flexbox() mixin includes -moz-box and the inline-flex() mixin includes -moz-inline-box, creating an inconsistency where Mozilla's legacy flexbox display is supported but the corresponding alignment property is not. This could cause alignment issues in older Firefox versions that use the -moz-box display model.
